_comment: Ground truth for the detection corpus. THIS FILE IS THE SPEC; the analyzer is the
thing under test. Every `expect` entry is derived from the Docker image tag (or from
a command run INSIDE the container via `exec_probes`), never from what the analyzer
happens to report. `docker run nginx:1.25.3` is Nginx 1.25.3 by definition -- that is
the only reason this corpus is trustworthy as a scoreboard.
Every `technology` value below was checked against wappalyzer_cache.json before being
written here: an expectation naming a technology the database does not define can never
pass, it can only drag the floor down for no reason.
DELIBERATELY ABSENT IMAGES: traefik, prom/prometheus, hashicorp/consul and
hashicorp/vault were pulled and then skipped. The shipped database (7,586 technologies)
has no entry for Traefik, Prometheus, Consul or Vault -- grep wappalyzer_cache.json and
you will find nothing. There is no expectation that could be written for them that the
engine is even capable of satisfying, so capturing them would add bytes and noise
without adding signal. Re-add them the day those technologies land in the database.

fixtures.name: nginx-1.25.3
fixtures.notes: Stock nginx welcome page. Simplest possible case: the version is in the Server header.

fixtures.name: httpd-2.4.58
fixtures.notes: Stock Apache 'It works!' page. The official httpd image leaves ServerTokens at its default (Full), so the Server header carries the full version.

fixtures.name: grafana-10.2.3
fixtures.notes: GET / redirects to /login; the captured page is the unauthenticated login screen.

fixtures.name: gitea-1.21.3
fixtures.notes: INSTALLER PAGE. With no database configured Gitea redirects / to /install. That page is still served by Gitea and still carries its fingerprints, but it is NOT a running forge -- do not read a miss here as 'Gitea is undetectable on real sites'.

fixtures.name: wordpress-6.4.2
fixtures.notes: INSTALLER PAGE. Without MySQL, / redirects to /wp-admin/install.php (the 'choose your language' step). The meta generator and the wp-admin asset paths are present; a real site's theme/plugin fingerprints are not.

fixtures.name: drupal-10.2.1
fixtures.notes: INSTALLER PAGE. / redirects to /core/install.php. NOTE for whoever reads the version score: Drupal's meta generator only ever emits the MAJOR version ('Drupal 10'), so an exact match against 10.2.1 is not achievable from HTML alone -- the test scores that as a PARTIAL match on purpose.

fixtures.name: joomla-5.0.2
fixtures.notes: INSTALLER PAGE, captured with the image's ENTRYPOINT DELIBERATELY BYPASSED. The joomla entrypoint runs makedb.php first and refuses to hand over to Apache until a MySQL server answers, so the stock `docker run joomla:5.0.2-apache` exits before serving anything and a database sidecar would be the only alternative. The cmd below does exactly what the entrypoint does for the web root -- copies /usr/src/joomla verbatim into /var/www/html -- and then starts Apache, so the page captured is the unmodified Joomla 5.0.2 installer as shipped in the image. Nothing about the served files is synthesised; only the database wait is skipped.

fixtures.name: nextcloud-28.0.1
fixtures.notes: SETUP PAGE. With no database configured Nextcloud serves the first-run setup wizard. Nextcloud sets several cookies on this page, which is exactly why set_cookie_headers is captured as a list rather than a joined string.

fixtures.name: mediawiki-1.41.0
fixtures.notes: SETUP PAGE. Without LocalSettings.php MediaWiki serves mw-config/index.php (the installer).

fixtures.name: jenkins-2.440
fixtures.notes: Jenkins answers an unauthenticated / with 403 and its 'Authentication required' page until the first-run setup wizard is unlocked, so that 403 -- headers and all -- is what this fixture holds. That is a realistic capture: a locked-down Jenkins on the public internet looks exactly like this. Jetty is expected WITHOUT a version because the image tag pins Jenkins, not the bundled servlet container; the response happens to name a Jetty version in its Server header, but a ground-truth file must not take the target's word for anything, so no version is asserted.

expect.source: bundled servlet container; version not pinned by the image tag

fixtures.name: sonarqube-10.3
fixtures.notes: SonarQube boots an embedded Elasticsearch before it listens, so it is the slowest fixture in the corpus by a wide margin. The tag pins the MINOR version only (10.3), so the recorded ground-truth version is '10.3'.
